verification.final_statement: In the GStreamer 1.26 videorate source (gstvideorate.c), default (non-drop-only) mode keeps the previous input buffer in prevbuf. It outputs that buffer via gst_buffer_ref (videorate->prevbuf) followed by gst_buffer_make_writable ('make sure we can write to the metadata'). Because prevbuf still holds a reference, this makes a new GstBuffer. Per the GstBuffer documentation, that copy shares (references) the underlying memory unless the memory type requires a copy. The output PTS is then rewritten to the output-grid timestamp. In drop-only mode the input buffer is held in prevbuf only during the chain call and cleared before it returns. If kept, the buffer is pushed by GstBaseTransform itself ('This avoids storing extra reference to the buffer'). Its PTS is not rewritten, but videorate still sets OFFSET/OFFSET_END and the DISCONT/GAP flags on that same buffer. When a fixed output framerate is negotiated, it also sets DURATION to the output frame period.

claims.statement: REASONING: For OQ-131 (60 to 30 fps live), videorate with caps framerate=30/1 and drop-only=true drops alternate frames with no added latency and no stored reference (M-54, M-55); default mode adds one input-frame of latency (1/60 s = 16.7 ms at 60 fps input; 1/50 s = 20 ms at 50 fps) and holds one capture buffer reference (M-54, M-55). drop-only does not rewrite PTS, so output keeps source timestamps (M-55).
claims.source_title: Reasoning over claims M-52 to M-55
claims.evidence: Inputs: M-52, M-53, M-54, M-55. Arithmetic: 1 s / 60 = 16.67 ms; 1 s / 50 = 20 ms.

verification.final_statement: REASONING: For OQ-131 (60 to 30 fps live), consider videorate with output caps framerate=30/1 and drop-only=true. It passes an input frame only when the frame's PTS is at or after the next 1/30 s output slot. With a steady 60 fps input it therefore passes about every other frame; the exact pattern depends on input PTS jitter relative to the 1/30 s grid. In this mode it reports no added latency, decides each frame within the same chain call and keeps no buffer reference between calls (M-54, M-55). Default (non-drop-only) mode instead adds one input-frame period to the latency query: 1/60 s ≈ 16.67 ms at 60 fps input, or 1/50 s = 20 ms at 50 fps input. It also keeps one captured buffer referenced in prevbuf between calls (M-54, M-55). In drop-only mode videorate does not rewrite PTS, so output buffers keep the source PTS. It does, however, set DURATION to the output frame period (1/30 s ≈ 33.33 ms) and rewrite OFFSET/OFFSET_END (M-55).
verification.notes: Re-derived the reasoning from the 1.26 source. Drop-only decision (transform_ip): 'if ((videorate->segment.rate > 0.0 && in_ts >= videorate->next_ts) ...) res = gst_video_rate_push_buffer (...) else videorate->drop++;'. next_ts then advances on the fixed grid 'base_ts + out_frame_count * to_rate_denominator * GST_SECOND / to_rate_numerator'. So with ideal 60 fps PTS, frames 0, 2, 4... pass; with jittered capture PTS, a frame slightly before a slot is dropped and the next one passes, so the pattern is approximately, not strictly, alternate. Latency per the M-54 handler: from_rate_denominator/from_rate_numerator seconds. Arithmetic: 1/60 s = 16.666... ms; 1/50 s = 20 ms; 1/30 s = 33.333... ms. The grid slot is computed with gst_util_uint64_scale, which rounds down, so durations are 33,333,333 ns twice then 33,333,334 ns in each 3-frame cycle. Default mode holds prevbuf between calls (gst_video_rate_swap_prev / gst_buffer_replace). Drop-only clears prevbuf before returning. Corrections: 'output keeps source timestamps' is true for PTS only (DURATION/OFFSET are rewritten), and 'drops alternate frames' is only approximately true. Extra caution not in the claim: in non-skip-to-first mode, next_ts starts at the segment start (base_ts = segment.start at the SEGMENT event). If the first captured PTS were far from the segment start, drop-only would pass every frame until the 1/30 s grid caught up. skip-to-first=true anchors the grid at the first buffer's PTS instead (lines 1791-1795).
